name: dsh-focus-free-shortcuts
description: Local runtime patch: make the right-Sidebar pane commands (fullscreen primary+alt+Enter, split primary+Backslash), the double-Escape turn stop, and the approval panel's Enter/Escape decision fire without first clicking into the pane, the composer, or the approval card. Every bundled owner resolves its target from the keydown event target, and a keydown is dispatched to the focused element (or <body> when nothing is focused), so all of them silently decline until the user focuses the exact region: `pane.fullscreen.toggle` / `pane.split` call SidebarRight.focusedTarget(element) and return command.noFocus; the fixed `response.stop` sequence requires its target inside [data-conversation-session] / [data-conversation-region]; and the approval panel answers only while document.activeElement sits inside [data-approval-key] — which the composer takeover removes when it hides the composer bar, so focus falls back to <body> and both Enter and Escape lose their owner. This plugin opens its own fixed-input observer — the channel that runs for every keydown before configurable dispatch and can consume the press — and resolves the same owner without DOM focus: SidebarRight.commandTarget()'s active-dock-pane fallback for the pane commands, the main-view Session for the stop (`sessions.list.byId[id].retainedBy.mainView > 0`, the same fact UiSession uses), and that Session's published `pendingInteraction` approval for Enter/Escape (`answer('allowed-once' | 'rejected')`, the operation the panel buttons call). It consumes a press only when it actually acts, and stands down whenever the bundled owner owns that press (focused pane, conversation region, `[data-approval-key]` subtree), so exactly one owner remains per press. Nothing is registered in the shortcut catalog: no default bindings, no conflicts, no settings edits — and because each bridge follows the effective catalog row or the mounted fixed row, a rebound, unbound, or absent bundled command is left alone (an unmounted approval plugin removes approval.allow / approval.reject and the approval bridge becomes a no-op). Pane keys are Web-runtime only: Desktop dispatches configurable bindings from its native bridge, where a DOM-side consume cannot suppress the bundled press; the stop and approval keys are fixed actions and install on both runtimes. It also adds one brand-new key, Ctrl+Alt+J, that jumps the keyboard back to the composer: nothing bundled owns that combination, so the plugin mounts its own fixed row (dsh-focus-free-shortcuts.focus-composer) and, on the same fixed-input channel, resolves the main-view Session's input facade (`conversation.input.for(scope).focus()`, the same caret-restoring focus the application uses after an overlay) and consumes the press. It also adds one brand-new key pair, Ctrl+Alt+ArrowLeft / Ctrl+Alt+ArrowRight, that steps the Right Sidebar's shown page: one mounted fixed row (dsh-focus-free-shortcuts.page-cycle) reserves both arrows, the bridge reads the on-screen Session's pages through the public Sidebar face (`tabsIn` / `active()` / `focus(tabId)`, the same recorded operation a chip click runs), and after the switch hands the keyboard to the page the commit shows (locating the active pane one animation frame later, and only filling in when the page did not focus itself, so a terminal keeps its own focus). Unlike the other groups it deliberately accepts every input region, including a focused terminal, and ignores `defaultPrevented`, because the pair must keep working from inside the page it is about to leave; it stands down only for composing input, an autorepeat flood, a modal, a collapsed column, or a switch with no target page.
